title: Cartier Gysin normalization in the signed relative Kummer model
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, $m=\ell^n$, and $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z$. Let $X$ be a Noetherian excellent regular affine scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-regular-scheme], and let $f\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a nonzerodivisor such that the effective Cartier divisor $D=V(f)$ is regular [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Write $i:D\hookrightarrow X$ and $j:U=X-D\hookrightarrow X$. Work on small etale derived categories with $\Lambda_X(1)=\mu_{m,X}$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. Let $\kappa(f)\in H^1(U,\mu_m)$ be the class of the $\mu_m$-torsor of $m$-th roots of $f|_U$, equivalently the Kummer connecting class [lem-amb-kummer-any-base, lem-sc-torsor-h1]. Put $H^q_D(X,\mu_m)=H^q(R\Gamma_D(X,\mu_m))$ [def-pur-etale-derived-supported-sections]. Fix the signed relative realization of [def-amb-relative-etale-cohomology, lem-pur-divisor-torsor-boundary-signs]: on an injective resolution $J$ its differential is $D(a,b)=(da,\operatorname{res}(a)-db)$ on $J^q(X)\oplus J^{q-1}(U)$ and its localization boundary $\partial:H^1(U,\mu_m)\to H^2_D(X,\mu_m)$ is represented by $b\mapsto(0,-b)$. Use the Yoneda convention for the supported Chern class of a line bundle $B$ with an invertible section $s$ on $U$: its degree-one supported extension has fibre over the supported generator equal to the frame torsor of $B$, with the specified frame $s$ sent to zero, and its degree-two class is the Yoneda product with the Kummer extension. This specifies the Chern normalization allowed in Expose XVI, Definition 1.1 and its sign footnote. Under the supported-Hom and closed-adjunction identifications [lem-amb-closed-support-hom], the Gabber Gysin morphism of [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity], twisted and shifted as $\operatorname{Cl}_i(1)[2]:\Lambda_D\to i^!\Lambda_X(1)[2]$, corresponds to
$$-\partial\kappa(f)\in H^2_D(X,\mu_m).$$
This assertion fixes the comparison with the stated signed relative realization; the minus sign is part of the assertion.

source.place: Expose XVI, sections 2.1–2.3: Definition 2.1.1, Definitions 2.2.2.5 and 2.2.2.7 (rank one), Definition 2.3.1; comparison with the explicitly specified signed relative Kummer realization. The signed-relative comparison is agent-stated, not a verbatim assertion of XVII Proposition 2.4.2.1(a).
